# Security, privacy, backup, and restore {#sec-security}

## Security and privacy

Use approved public, synthetic, or authorized clinical data. Keep PHI, private DICOM headers, model weights, tokens, passwords, CVAT credentials, runtime SQLite files, and local-state directories out of Git and screenshots. Original source images are immutable.

The product is a research and clinical-support proof of concept. Human review remains authoritative. No product claim establishes regulatory approval, autonomous diagnosis, referral, treatment, or calibrated probability.

## Backup

Back up the active Workspace SQLite database, approved export packages, Workspace configuration, and the exact release/configuration record according to hospital policy. Keep model assets with their verified hashes and preserve the relationship between release, model assets, and exports.

Do not back up or copy secret files into the repository. Store `/etc/dr-support/model-server.env` through the hospital secret-management process.

## Restore

1. Stop the affected service or workstation process.
2. Restore the Workspace database and approved export package to a controlled path.
3. Restore the same release or a validated compatible release.
4. Verify file ownership and permissions.
5. Run the model asset verification and `/health` checks.
6. Open the workstation, inspect the Workspace, and confirm source and annotation hashes before resuming review.

## CVAT

CVAT Online is optional. Keep `CVAT_TOKEN` only in secure runtime configuration. Do not paste it into commands, browser JavaScript, screenshots, documentation, or issue reports. Ambiguous remote writes require manual reconciliation; never retry blindly.
